key_insight: Learn the dissipation potential with an input-convex neural network so the resulting constitutive law remains physically well-posed, even for indirect velocity-only data.
engineering_relevance: This gives a robust way to identify complex-fluid models that generalize to new geometries and avoid unstable or nonphysical PDE behavior.
method: Use an input-convex neural architecture (ICNNE) to enforce convexity by design.
Impose frame-indifference and evenness in the second strain-rate invariant through symmetrization.
Add a penalty to make the potential dissipative by encouraging zero gradient at the origin; train with Firedrake + PyTorch coupling.
evidence_signal: The approach is tested on four settings—compressible Navier-Stokes, Herschel-Bulkley, Hibler sea-ice, and DEM data—and the learned potentials recover known physics, transfer to unseen geometries, and remain stable where unstructured methods diverge.
watch_item: The method relies on careful PDE-constrained optimization and penalty tuning, so training stability and implementation complexity may limit adoption.
paper_title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
